entries.title: CIP-0001: CIP Process
entries.summary: Read proposal status and implementation evidence as separate claims.

facts.text: The CIP process defines proposal states and review requirements.
A CIP can specify an ecosystem convention rather than a ledger change.

designNotes: Our admission policy records sources, executable evidence and unknowns independently.

guarantees: A public, versioned design record
doesNotGuarantee: Wallet adoption or deployment merely from a numbered document

lifecycle: Implementations and revisions require separate tracking
risks: Treating Proposed as a hard-fork activation
Confusing an implementor list with independent acceptance testing
interoperability: Pin the source revision and exact status string; inactive reasons matter.
opportunities: Make every Studio capability display its strongest demonstrated evidence, not a marketing maturity badge.

entries.title: CIP-0008: Message Signing
entries.summary: Prove control of a signing key with structured messages, then separately establish the requested entitlement.

facts.text: CIP-8 specifies Cardano message signatures using COSE structures.
The signed payload and public-key material can be verified independently of sending a transaction.

designNotes: Use origin, action, asset identity, nonce and short expiry in the challenge. Never interpret a message signature as blanket mint authorization.

guarantees: Integrity and signer-key evidence for the checked message

risks: Trusting stake identity as ownership of every payment address
interoperability: CIP-30 signData connects this format to compatible wallets; real wallet/address forms must be tested.
opportunities: Transfer-aware member workspaces with public authentication receipts and private content delivery.

entries.title: CIP-0014: User-Facing Asset Fingerprint
entries.summary: Show a compact human identifier while retaining the exact native-asset identity.

facts.text: The fingerprint uses a 160-bit BLAKE2b digest of policy-ID bytes concatenated with asset-name bytes, encoded as Bech32 with the asset prefix.

designNotes: Keep fingerprint functions separate from authorization comparisons.

guarantees: Deterministic display fingerprint

lifecycle: Display alongside policy and asset-name hex
risks: Hashing the textual hex instead of decoded bytes
interoperability: Display fingerprints are useful across explorers; lookup systems still need full policy/name bytes.
opportunities: An identity inspector that shows Unicode, raw bytes, labels and fingerprint together.

entries.title: CIP-0019: Cardano Addresses
entries.summary: Separate payment authority, staking authority and network in address handling.

facts.text: Cardano address forms encode payment and sometimes staking credentials; credentials can refer to keys or scripts.
Enterprise and base addresses have different structures.

designNotes: Make supported address types a declared builder capability; reject unsupported forms before balancing.

guarantees: Explicit credential and network encoding
doesNotGuarantee: That a stake-key signature can spend a payment-key output

risks: Accepting a reward address as an NFT recipient
Assuming every address belongs to a key wallet
interoperability: Script wallets and base addresses need different signing and change treatment.
opportunities: Human-readable authority maps for creator, holder and updater addresses.

entries.title: CIP-0021: Transaction requirements for interoperability with hardware wallets
entries.summary: Hardware-wallet acceptance is a byte-serialization and transaction-shape requirement.

facts.text: CIP-21 specifies transaction restrictions and serialization rules intended to support hardware-wallet interoperability.

designNotes: Add hardware checks as an independent preflight profile without silently rewriting an approved body.

guarantees: A target profile for supported serialized transactions
doesNotGuarantee: That every hardware model or firmware accepts a compliant-looking transaction

risks: Changing serialized transaction bytes after review
interoperability: Record wallet model, firmware, connector and transaction class in the acceptance matrix.
opportunities: Export a reproducible device-acceptance fixture for every mint template.

entries.title: CIP-0025: Media Token Metadata Standard
entries.summary: Attach recognizable media metadata to positive token issuance.

facts.text: CIP-25 uses transaction metadata label 721 for assets minted with positive quantity.
Version 1 uses textual policy/name keys; version 2 uses byte-string keys.
The schema requires name and image and supports typed file attachments.

designNotes: Measure actual complete signed bytes. Preserve immutable originals and publish hashes of recovered content.

guarantees: A common media description when consumers follow the specification

risks: Metadata spoofing where a policy does not constrain issuer-controlled metadata
interoperability: Viewer support for data URIs, MIME types and HTML differs; embedding a file does not require a wallet to execute it.

maturity.version: Metadata v1 and v2; explicit key encoding required

opportunities: A byte-budget compiler that chooses a representation and proves exact chain recovery.

entries.title: CIP-0027: CNFT Community Royalties Standard
entries.summary: Publish a collection royalty convention and disclose who actually honors it.

facts.text: CIP-27 publishes royalty information through transaction metadata under label 777.

designNotes: Show descriptive royalties separately from transaction-enforced payments.

guarantees: Discoverable royalty terms for cooperating consumers
doesNotGuarantee: Royalty collection on all token transfers

interoperability: Support must be observed at the actual trading venue, including sales outside its contracts.
opportunities: Royalty observatory comparing declared terms with demonstrated marketplace behavior.

entries.title: CIP-0029: Phase-1 Monetary Scripts Serialization Formats
entries.summary: Native policies compose key-signature and time predicates; they do not execute application logic.

facts.text: Phase-1 scripts support signature, all/any/threshold combinations and validity-time constraints.
Script serialization contributes to the script hash used by native policies.

designNotes: A real one-shot policy needs a consumed seed or equivalently enforced state; label native timed editions honestly.

guarantees: Configured signature and time conditions on minting-policy execution
doesNotGuarantee: One-shot issuance from a signature-plus-expiry policy

risks: Closing future burning together with minting
Claiming lifetime uniqueness from one observed mint
interoperability: Native scripts are distinct from Plutus and do not require a Plutus datum/redeemer path.
opportunities: Policy lifecycle simulator showing whether minting, burning and recovery remain possible at each time.

entries.title: CIP-0030: Cardano dApp-Wallet Web Bridge
entries.summary: Use explicit wallet consent and verify the exact transaction that the wallet signs.

facts.text: CIP-30 defines the browser dApp-wallet bridge including enable, UTxO/address reads, signData, signTx and submitTx.
signTx returns a transaction witness set; extension support is negotiated.

designNotes: Bind an automation plan to hashes and require wallet review of the concrete unsigned transaction.

guarantees: A standard request surface and returned signature material
doesNotGuarantee: That a request was confirmed on chain
That the app can safely mutate signed bytes

risks: Ambiguous submission retried as a new mint
interoperability: Wallet injection timing, mobile browser support, hardware profiles and extensions vary.
opportunities: Agent-assisted mint preparation with a wallet-owned final approval step and verifiable receipt.

entries.title: CIP-0031: Reference inputs
entries.summary: Read another UTxO in a transaction without consuming it.

facts.text: Reference inputs expose existing UTxO data to scripts without spending that output.
They do not provide input value to balance the transaction.

designNotes: Separate read-only metadata references from consumed authorization/state inputs.

guarantees: Read access to a referenced output during validation
doesNotGuarantee: Persistent availability after a concurrent spend

risks: Using an NFT in a reference input as proof of spending authority
Assuming read sharing eliminates state-write contention
interoperability: Scripts and builders must use an era/language that supports reference inputs.
opportunities: Composable artifact libraries shared by many NFTs, with independently checked content commitments.

entries.title: CIP-0032: Inline datums
entries.summary: Carry datum bytes in the output so future consumers can retrieve state directly.

facts.text: Inline datums place the datum itself in a transaction output rather than only its hash.
Output storage requirements depend on datum size.

designNotes: Pin schema versions and reject unknown state transitions before requesting a signature.

guarantees: Datum availability with the output
doesNotGuarantee: Correct state semantics or authorized updates

risks: Confusing transaction metadata with Plutus data
Failing to supply valid continuing datum
interoperability: Old Plutus script versions have compatibility restrictions when inline datums appear.
opportunities: Portable state snapshots and offline-readable evolving collectibles.

entries.title: CIP-0033: Reference scripts
entries.summary: Reuse a script stored in an output instead of attaching it repeatedly.

facts.text: Reference scripts allow a transaction to use script bytes held in a referenced output.

designNotes: A library receipt should identify script hash, reference UTxO, fallback bytes and observed availability.

guarantees: Script availability through the specified unspent reference

interoperability: Budget with current ledger parameters and compatible script language, not the original proposal cost model alone.
opportunities: A public verified validator library with reproducible builds and replaceable distribution points.

entries.title: CIP-0040: Collateral Output
entries.summary: Return excess collateral rather than treating every collateral input as intended payment.

facts.text: CIP-40 introduces collateral return and total collateral fields for transactions that use collateral.

designNotes: Expose a separate collateral-at-risk line in every Plutus review.

guarantees: A way to specify collateral consumption and return under ledger rules
doesNotGuarantee: That a failing script costs nothing
That collateral is the normal transaction fee

interoperability: Check wallet collateral API and ledger-era support together.
opportunities: A loss-envelope analyzer for automated transaction preparation.

entries.title: CIP-0054: Cardano Smart NFTs
entries.summary: A proposed viewer API for NFTs that read chain data or share renderer code.

facts.text: CIP-54 proposes a JavaScript NFT API and metadata declarations for transaction data, token data and shared renderers.

designNotes: Implement a small explicit read-only host bridge and deterministic offline fixtures before optional viewer integrations.

guarantees: An interoperable interface if the viewer implements the proposal

risks: Executing untrusted code with wallet privileges
interoperability: The proposal remains Proposed. Do not label an arbitrary embedded HTML NFT CIP-54 compliant.
opportunities: Shared on-chain engines with compact per-token cartridges and reproducible playback.

entries.title: CIP-0057: Plutus Contract Blueprint
entries.summary: Make the validator interface machine-readable for builders, inspectors and agents.

facts.text: CIP-57 defines a Plutus contract blueprint including interfaces, schemas and compiled-validator information.

designNotes: Generate bounded MCP inputs and human explanations from a reviewed blueprint; deny arbitrary contract execution by default.

guarantees: A structured description of the declared contract interface
doesNotGuarantee: Deployed behavior matching a prose promise

risks: Treating a blueprint as proof of correctness
Wrong parameter order or CBOR wrapper
interoperability: Schema consumers must support the exact blueprint version and data encoding.
opportunities: Self-describing mint capabilities with reproducible validator identities.

entries.title: CIP-0060: Music Token Metadata
entries.summary: Describe songs and releases so music players can discover the right credits and audio.

facts.text: CIP-60 extends CIP-25 and CIP-68 with music-specific release and song metadata.
The current document links v3 CDDL and marks v1/v2 CDDL deprecated.

designNotes: Keep immutable program/seed identity alongside a separately rendered track with honest composition and master credits.

guarantees: Structured music discovery for supporting consumers

risks: Treating a generative synthesizer as a fixed recording without describing that distinction
interoperability: Record the chosen version. Resolve boolean and field-type representation against CDDL and actual ledger encoding before claiming conformance.

maturity.version: Current v3 CDDL; v1/v2 deprecated in upstream README

opportunities: A standards-aware generative album whose players can export reproducible audio plus source.

entries.title: CIP-0067: Asset Name Label Registry
entries.summary: Prefix asset-name bytes with a checksummed purpose label.

facts.text: CIP-67 allocates a four-byte asset-name prefix containing a 16-bit label and CRC-8 checksum.
The registered prefix consumes four of the available asset-name bytes.

designNotes: Surface both interpreted label and exact raw identity; reserve at most 28 bytes for content under this prefix.

guarantees: A parseable label when the prefix and checksum are valid

risks: Counting characters instead of encoded bytes
interoperability: The source status is Proposed despite use by Active CIP-68; status and actual integration must remain separate.
opportunities: A standards identity workbench with official vectors and malformed-prefix diagnostics.

entries.title: CIP-0068: Datum Metadata Standard
entries.summary: Separate transferable user tokens from authenticated datum-backed metadata.

facts.text: CIP-68 pairs user tokens with a reference NFT under the same policy and naming relationship.
The reference output carries constructor 0 with metadata, version and extra fields.
Current text includes direct metadata versions and a v4 nested 721 format.

designNotes: Use a reviewed one-shot mint and state validator with bounded fields; record updater, recovery and freeze semantics separately.

guarantees: A discoverable datum representation when identity rules are followed

lifecycle: Freeze or recover by explicit rules
interoperability: Defaulting to a newer representation without viewer evidence can break consumers. Match label, policy, name bytes and supported datum version.

maturity.version: Direct versions 1–3; nested format version 4 in pinned text

opportunities: Living scientific instruments, evolving art and transferable creator workspaces with auditable state history.

entries.title: CIP-0071: Non-Fungible Token (NFT) Proxy Voting Standard
entries.summary: A proposed NFT-ballot design for collection-specific on-chain votes.

facts.text: CIP-71 proposes one-time ballot tokens minted from NFT eligibility, datum votes and a ballot-box contract.

designNotes: Prove uniqueness across transactions and transfers, not only within one mint context.

guarantees: Ballot restrictions only to the extent validators enforce them
doesNotGuarantee: Complete counting from a partial indexer

lifecycle: Return or burn according to policy
interoperability: Collection polling is separate from Cardano constitutional governance; proposal status remains Proposed.
opportunities: Public reproducible collection decisions with proofs linking every counted ballot to its rule set.

entries.title: CIP-0086: NFT Metadata Update Oracles
entries.summary: An oracle-driven metadata history for existing CIP-25 assets without ordinary remint updates.

facts.text: CIP-86 proposes authorized metadata-oracle assignments and ordered updates under label 86.
It distinguishes main and update addresses and requires replaying updates in chain order with rollback handling.

designNotes: Use an experimental historical reader first. Preserve original CIP-25 and show the applied authority chain separately.

guarantees: Attributable updates if the consumer verifies assignment and signatures

risks: Prose mentions null deletion although ledger metadata has no null type
interoperability: Proposed status and spec inconsistencies require explicit profiles; do not silently retrofit frozen collections or overwrite original evidence.
opportunities: Museum-style provenance timelines for metadata evolution with visible administrator actions.

entries.title: CIP-0088: Token Policy Registration
entries.summary: Register policy intent and capabilities with verifiable policy-associated evidence.

facts.text: CIP-88 provides versioned policy registration with a numeric-field structure, witnesses and CIP-specific details.
Its aim includes declaring metadata standards and shared collection information.

designNotes: Combine declaration records with independent test receipts, and show disagreement rather than auto-trusting a registry entry.

guarantees: Authenticated declarations when the registration witness rules are checked
doesNotGuarantee: That advertised capabilities are implemented or safe

risks: Self-asserted capability promoted to verified feature
Confusing token-policy registration with unrelated extended uses
interoperability: Pin the root version and each CIP-detail schema independently; inspect actual witness semantics for the policy type.
opportunities: Machine-discoverable mint products and a public compatibility passport for every collection.

entries.title: CIP-0089: Distributed DApps & Beacon Tokens
entries.summary: Use authenticated beacon assets to discover distributed application state.

facts.text: CIP-89 describes per-user dApp addresses and beacon-token-based discovery of application UTxOs.

designNotes: For Studio use, design per-artifact state so independent holders avoid a single global write bottleneck.

guarantees: Recognizable state only when beacon policy and output rules authenticate it
doesNotGuarantee: That every similarly named token is valid
A complete query from a partial provider

interoperability: Read the actual application policy and datum schema; the pattern is broader than one universal wire format.
opportunities: Discoverable public remix requests, collaboration invitations and per-NFT service state.

entries.title: CIP-0093: Authenticated Web3 HTTP requests
entries.summary: A proposed structured request-authentication payload for wallet signatures.

facts.text: CIP-93 defines structured payloads and processing guidance for authenticating HTTP requests with Cardano wallet signatures.

designNotes: A minting MCP service should scope authority by method and immutable plan, not grant account-wide powers from login.

guarantees: Integrity of the exact signed request under checked keys and schema

risks: Omitting method, origin or action binding
Serving private content from a public URL
interoperability: The standard is Proposed; support and cryptographic/address verification require acceptance tests.
opportunities: A shared wallet-authentication layer for agent requests and holder services.

entries.title: CIP-0102: Royalty Datum Metadata
entries.summary: Describe datum-backed royalties that cooperating sale validators can read.

facts.text: CIP-102 defines royalty NFTs with label 500 and datum royalty recipients.
Current text supports v1 and v2; v2 adds numeric postfixes for multiple royalty policies within a collection.

designNotes: Ship a royalty decoder and transaction explainer before a royalty-bearing sale template.

guarantees: Readable royalty terms and enforceable payments inside a validator that checks them
doesNotGuarantee: Royalties on every free transfer or external sale

interoperability: Current source is Proposed and says its linked reference implementation covers v1. Use version-specific support claims.

maturity.version: v1; v2 intrapolicy royalties in current text

opportunities: Transparent collaborator splits with replayable sale-payment evidence.

entries.title: CIP-0103: Web-Wallet Bridge - Bulk transaction signing
entries.summary: Bulk signing can reduce prompts while each transaction keeps its own outcome.

facts.text: CIP-103 defines signTxs for arrays of independent or dependent transactions and matching witness-set order.
It also specifies a bulk submission method.

designNotes: Persist per-transaction attempt and inclusion state; a bulk UI is not an atomic ledger transaction.

guarantees: A negotiated interface for grouped signing
doesNotGuarantee: Atomic inclusion of an entire batch

lifecycle: Review total cost and every body
risks: Validity expiry during a long batch
interoperability: Feature-detect the extension and retain sequential signing and recovery.
opportunities: Recoverable edition and multipart publishing with one clear bounded approval packet.

entries.title: CIP-0106: Web-Wallet Bridge - Multisig wallets
entries.summary: Multisig wallets need asynchronous completion and native-script-aware requirements.

facts.text: CIP-106 proposes script-requirement discovery and unsigned-transaction submission/completion for multisig wallets.
Its profile disables ordinary signTx and signData.

designNotes: Keep a distinct transaction adapter with explicit capabilities and cancellation/expiry states.

guarantees: A proposed interface for gathering multisig authorization

lifecycle: Verify exact body and witness set
risks: Treating a script credential as a key hash
interoperability: Proposed and evolving; test the named wallet implementation instead of assuming CIP-30 interoperability.
opportunities: Co-created collections whose issuance requires collaborator quorum.

entries.title: CIP-0124: Extend token metadata for translations
entries.summary: Localize token descriptions while preserving a canonical fallback.

facts.text: CIP-124 proposes optional strings maps keyed by language-region cultures for collection and asset properties.
The proposal discusses on-chain and externally hosted translations.

designNotes: Declare which translations are embedded and hash external resources when appropriate; never translate identity bytes.

guarantees: Localized display in consumers implementing the agreed profile

interoperability: Proposed status; test a precise inline-object profile and retain canonical fields for older viewers.
opportunities: Multilingual museum labels and accessible instructions carried with the artwork.

entries.title: CIP-0141: Web-Wallet Bridge - Plutus wallets
entries.summary: Plutus wallets expose script-specific transaction requirements beyond key-wallet signing.

facts.text: CIP-141 proposes a wallet bridge for script-controlled wallets including requirements for inputs, references, datums and redeemers.
Its documented API version is 2.0.

designNotes: Allow only explicitly supported operations. Never forward arbitrary wallet-secret APIs through minting MCP.

guarantees: A way to express script-wallet requirements if implemented
doesNotGuarantee: Compatibility with a builder that only handles key inputs

risks: Secret-bearing extension methods exposed through generic agents
interoperability: Proposed status. A generic CIP-30 connection is insufficient evidence of script-wallet support.
opportunities: Future transferable studio accounts with bounded creator-agent permissions.

entries.title: CIP-0142: Web-Wallet Bridge - Network Determination
entries.summary: Distinguish specific test networks instead of treating all network-ID zero wallets alike.

facts.text: CIP-142 proposes api.cip142.getNetworkMagic because CIP-30 getNetworkId distinguishes mainnet from testnet but not individual testnets.

designNotes: Display full network identity in every plan and include it in cache keys and receipts.

guarantees: Additional network-magic identification from supporting wallets
doesNotGuarantee: That an unrelated provider is on the same chain

risks: Building with one testnet provider and another testnet wallet
interoperability: The proposal remains Proposed; explicit testnet selection and provider evidence are still needed where unsupported.
opportunities: Safe testnet laboratories for agents and human creators.

entries.title: CIP-0143: Interoperable Programmable Tokens
entries.summary: Retain this inactive design as prior art, not a live standalone token standard.

facts.text: The pinned CIP-143 frontmatter marks it Inactive and states incorporation into candidate CIP-0113.

designNotes: Keep inactive entries searchable so agents can explain why a tempting design was not selected.

guarantees: Traceable history of programmable-token design

lifecycle: Re-admit current design only with primary evidence
risks: Marketing restrictions as native NFT features
interoperability: Replacement-candidate status must be researched separately; this entry does not claim acceptance.
opportunities: A standards change monitor that prevents plans from depending on retired proposals.

entries.title: CIP-0158: Cardano URIs - Browse Application
entries.summary: Open a specific dApp URL in a compatible wallet browser.

facts.text: CIP-158 defines web+cardano://browse/v1?uri= followed by a percent-encoded target URI.

designNotes: Use deep links for app navigation, never as a claim that a mint has been authorized.

guarantees: Navigation semantics in registered supporting handlers
doesNotGuarantee: Transfer of local drafts or files

interoperability: Keep a visible ordinary HTTPS link and copy fallback; OS handler and wallet support vary.
opportunities: Physical exhibit cards and QR journeys that enter the exact creator or recovery view.

entries.title: CIP-0171: On-chain Smart Contract Bytecode Verification
entries.summary: Link on-chain script use to an exact source revision and compiler recipe.

facts.text: CIP-171 proposes label-1984 verification metadata containing compiler-specific source, commit, version and parameter information.
Its encoding chunks Plutus-data CBOR into ledger-sized byte strings.

designNotes: Treat source repositories as untrusted inputs; use offline/bounded reproducible builders and publish outputs rather than running code in MCP.

guarantees: A declared build recipe that independent tools can attempt to reproduce
doesNotGuarantee: A successful bytecode match until rebuilt

risks: Hash comparison without matching language version
interoperability: The proposal remains Proposed. Unknown compiler/schema constructors need defined handling.
opportunities: An inspectable contract passport connecting creator promises to exact deployed code.

entries.title: CIP-0186: Cardano Wallet Deep-Link Signing
entries.summary: A proposed mobile-native request/callback transport for Cardano wallet operations.

facts.text: CIP-186 proposes native-app wallet requests via OS links with ephemeral key exchange, callback binding and transaction-body commitments.

designNotes: Keep this behind an experimental transport boundary; do not hand-roll production cryptography from prose.

guarantees: Specified request/response binding when the full protocol is implemented
doesNotGuarantee: Compatibility from CIP-158 browse links alone

interoperability: Proposed; the implementor list is empty in the pinned frontmatter. Require actual device and wallet conformance tests.
opportunities: Native mobile Studio and agent-to-phone approval flows when ecosystem support is demonstrated.

entries.title: CIP-0188: Token-Owned Addresses
entries.summary: A proposed deterministic address whose spending authority follows an NFT consumed in the transaction.

facts.text: CIP-188 proposes a canonical Plutus V3 token-owned-address derivation.
Its spending rules require exactly one controlling asset in spent inputs and outputs with no mint/burn of that asset.
Self-deposit of the controlling NFT intentionally enables permissionless spending subject to ledger witnesses.

designNotes: Start with derivation and hazard analysis. For private vaults, refuse self-deposit and explain inherited control before accepting funds.

guarantees: The specified transaction-local controlling-asset conditions

interoperability: Proposed; canonical bytes and Plutus V3 parameter serialization determine the address. A similar custom vault is not automatically CIP-188.

maturity.version: TOA v1; canonical Plutus V3 byte derivation

opportunities: NFT-owned instruments, inventories and collaborative workspaces, after validator and wallet acceptance.

entries.title: CIP-0190: Proof of Existence Transaction Metadata
entries.summary: Anchor exact content commitments independently of minting a token.

facts.text: CIP-190 proposes label-309 content-hash records with optional signatures, storage references and supersedence.
The record commits to exact bytes; optional encrypted-content envelopes have their own algorithm profiles.

designNotes: Publish a clear separation between byte equality, ledger observation, optional author signatures and externally established rights.

guarantees: A verifiable recorded digest when inclusion and bytes are checked
doesNotGuarantee: Truth, authorship, ownership or legal rights from a digest alone

risks: Hashing normalized bytes while promising originals
Confusing encryption with privacy of public metadata
interoperability: The standard is Proposed. Minimal hash-only support must be labeled as a supported profile, not full cryptographic-envelope conformance.
opportunities: Proof-carrying artworks, scientific datasets and software releases with independent recovery kits.

entries.title: aiken-lang/aiken
entries.summary: A compiler and contract platform with a natural path to reviewed blueprint-driven mint templates.

facts.text: Aiken is a Cardano smart-contract platform whose upstream provides installation, tutorials, compiler source and releases.

designNotes: Retain this repository’s existing serialization for native paths; introduce new validator tooling through an isolated adapter.

guarantees: Reproducible outputs only with a pinned build environment

interoperability: Use the generated Plutus language version and schema in every builder; upstream HEAD is not the installed release.

maturity.standardStatus: Upstream repository; release is separately observed

opportunities: Small audited capability contracts with generated documentation and transaction fixtures.

entries.title: Emurgo/cardano-serialization-lib
entries.summary: Use exact Cardano serialization as a cross-check around builders and wallet witnesses.

facts.text: Cardano Serialization Lib provides Rust and JavaScript/WASM serialization and deserialization for Cardano data structures.

designNotes: Keep digest and semantic verification separate: an identical body can still encode the wrong destination.

guarantees: Byte-level construction and decoding under the selected library version

interoperability: Record exact package versions and supported era; verify browser and Node fixtures where both are used.

maturity.standardStatus: Upstream repository; release is separately observed

opportunities: Reusable transaction inspection and byte-accurate mint sizing through UI and MCP.

entries.title: Anastasia-Labs/lucid-evolution
entries.summary: A TypeScript off-chain framework to evaluate as an adapter for Plutus transaction assembly.

facts.text: Lucid Evolution is an upstream transaction-builder and off-chain framework repository with separately released workspace packages.

designNotes: Treat a new SDK as a replaceable builder implementation, not a replacement for the application’s authorization rules.

guarantees: Convenient transaction construction under its supported APIs
doesNotGuarantee: That every workspace package shares the repository latest-release version

entries.title: Living Artifact: transferable state with a verifiable history
entries.summary: An NFT instrument or artwork whose allowed evolution is explicit and replayable.
designNotes: Original BEACN design proposal; no novelty, deployment or security-audit claim.
A one-shot issuer binds exactly one reference token to the corresponding user token.
Every update consumes authenticated current state and creates one continuing output with conserved reference token.
Holder control must be proven through an authorized spend or the explicitly chosen updater; reference-only possession is insufficient.
Separate human title, metadata schema version, application state version and monotonic revision.

guarantees: None until the stated mechanism is implemented and tested.
doesNotGuarantee: A metadata declaration does not implement this capability.

lifecycle: Freeze or recover under declared rules
risks: Concurrent updates race for the same state UTxO.
A privileged updater can change future state unless the validator constrains it.
Unbounded state grows fees and can make updates unbuildable.
interoperability: Publish the exact supported standard versions, viewer behavior and fallback path.
opportunities: Music machines whose approved patches change sound while historical versions stay recoverable.
Scientific instrument NFTs carrying calibration/reproducibility records without claiming measurements are truthful.

entries.title: Artifact Passport: claims accompanied by reproducible evidence
entries.summary: A portable manifest that lets a viewer inspect identity, bytes, contract build and demonstrated compatibility.
designNotes: Original BEACN design proposal; no novelty, deployment or security-audit claim.
Use separate fields for declared capabilities, observed tests and independently verified evidence.
Bind file hashes to a manifest, exact asset identity, transaction hash and source revision.
A hash proves byte agreement; it does not prove authorship, ownership or safety.
Unknown or stale evidence remains visible rather than becoming a pass.

guarantees: None until the stated mechanism is implemented and tested.
doesNotGuarantee: A metadata declaration does not implement this capability.

risks: Self-issued attestations can look authoritative if the UI hides issuer identity.
A receipt without referenced bytes cannot reproduce the claim.
interoperability: Publish the exact supported standard versions, viewer behavior and fallback path.
opportunities: An exhibit mode where every impressive demonstration has a corresponding downloadable proof kit.
Agent-readable compatibility passports for collectors and integrators.

entries.title: Shared Cartridges: immutable engines and compact named inputs
entries.summary: Reuse pinned program bytes across many collectibles while keeping each creation independently recoverable.
designNotes: Original BEACN design proposal; no novelty, deployment or security-audit claim.
An application manifest commits to every code/data dependency by digest and exact identity.
The renderer receives only a read-only bounded bridge; no wallet object, arbitrary fetch proxy or host origin.
All dependencies have a downloadable offline recovery path.
Claim only supported viewer APIs; a custom bridge must not be mislabeled as CIP-54 conformance.

guarantees: None until the stated mechanism is implemented and tested.
doesNotGuarantee: A metadata declaration does not implement this capability.

risks: Circular or unbounded dependency graphs exhaust resources.
Old code may remain vulnerable forever; safe viewers need independent controls.
interoperability: Publish the exact supported standard versions, viewer behavior and fallback path.
opportunities: Generative instruments, parameterized games and educational simulations sharing a compact verified engine.

entries.title: One-use Claims: an entitlement with an irreversible consumed state
entries.summary: Tickets and redemptions whose repeat-use rules survive reload, transfer and concurrency.
designNotes: Original BEACN design proposal; no novelty, deployment or security-audit claim.
Choose a burnable entitlement or authenticated state transition; never rely on a browser-local redeemed flag.
Verify exact asset identity, claimant authority, destination and quantity together.
If issuance has a closed native timelock, later burning under that policy is also closed.
Physical fulfillment remains an issuer process with separate terms and evidence.

guarantees: None until the stated mechanism is implemented and tested.
doesNotGuarantee: A metadata declaration does not implement this capability.

lifecycle: Handle fulfillment failure under explicit rules
risks: Administrator overrides contradicting a one-use claim.
interoperability: Publish the exact supported standard versions, viewer behavior and fallback path.
opportunities: Event passes that leave public verifiable used-state without publishing attendee personal data.

entries.title: Agent Mint Contract: bounded preparation with explicit wallet authority
entries.summary: Bots discover templates, prepare inspectable plans and return the exact transaction to its owner for signing.
designNotes: Original BEACN design proposal; no novelty, deployment or security-audit claim.
Treat tool inputs and knowledge text as untrusted data, not instructions.
Use finite template IDs and bounded parameters; exclude arbitrary shell, private-key, URL-fetch and file-read tools.
Bind approval to network, complete body hash, destination, mint map, asset/content hashes, fee ceiling and expiry.
Signing and submission are distinct from planning; record intent before any permitted broadcast.
An ambiguous broadcast is resolved by the original transaction hash, not a replacement transaction.

guarantees: None until the stated mechanism is implemented and tested.
doesNotGuarantee: A metadata declaration does not implement this capability.

risks: A signed transaction modified after review.
interoperability: Publish the exact supported standard versions, viewer behavior and fallback path.
opportunities: A reproducible public MCP that can create supported NFT artifacts without becoming a custodial signer.

entries.title: NFT Inventory: assets whose control follows a collectible
entries.summary: Explore the proposed token-owned-address model through derivation and hazard analysis before accepting value.
designNotes: Original BEACN design proposal; no novelty, deployment or security-audit claim.
Prove controlling-asset lifetime uniqueness independently of the transaction-local vault predicate.
Derive the exact canonical proposed address from pinned bytes; custom variants need separate identity.
Refuse depositing the controller into its own private inventory and explain inherited escrow/lending authority.
Show authority graphs and reject or flag cycles before nested inventory operations.

guarantees: None until the stated mechanism is implemented and tested.
doesNotGuarantee: A metadata declaration does not implement this capability.

lifecycle: Obtain independent review before funded use
risks: Self-deposit makes the canonical proposed vault permissionless.
Multiple controlling tokens enable competing authority.
Marketplace escrow may gain inventory-spending power.
interoperability: Publish the exact supported standard versions, viewer behavior and fallback path.
opportunities: Collectible synthesizers holding sample licenses or creator tools with transferable inventories.

entries.title: Session to Artifact: interactive computation with auditable final results
entries.summary: Use a fast session mechanism for interaction and publish a recoverable final artifact with a clear trust boundary.
designNotes: Original BEACN design proposal; no novelty, deployment or security-audit claim.
Distinguish local simulation, accepted Head transactions and observed L1 settlement.
Commit rules, seed/input transcript and evaluator version before claiming reproducible outcomes.
Publish participant assumptions, dispute window and recovery behavior.
A deterministic replay proves consistency with supplied inputs, not that external inputs were honest.

guarantees: None until the stated mechanism is implemented and tested.
doesNotGuarantee: A metadata declaration does not implement this capability.

risks: Misleading L1 permanence claims for transient session events.
interoperability: Publish the exact supported standard versions, viewer behavior and fallback path.
opportunities: Competitive generative performances ending with verifiable musical or visual artifacts.

entries.title: Standards Observatory: public evidence that improves with every implementation
entries.summary: Turn the knowledge base into an executable research pipeline with reviewable changes.
designNotes: Original BEACN design proposal; no novelty, deployment or security-audit claim.
Admit claims only with pinned primary evidence or explicitly labeled design reasoning.
Store conflicting normative text, examples and observed behavior in an issue register.
Use checked vectors and adversarial fixtures as executable knowledge.
Refresh sources into review candidates; source changes cannot automatically enable mint capabilities.

guarantees: None until the stated mechanism is implemented and tested.
doesNotGuarantee: A metadata declaration does not implement this capability.

Automatically importing third-party instructions into tool authority.
Source activity mistaken for audited maturity.
